analysis: The code snippet contains two calls to `String.substring`. The first call `msg.substring(START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX)` is executed when `end == -1` (no space in message). This call can throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` is negative or greater than the length of `msg`. The second call `message.substring(START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX, end)` is executed when `end != -1`. It can throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` is negative, if `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX > end`, or if `end` exceeds the length of `message`. The code does not validate the value of `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` (a constant, but its exact value is unknown and could be problematic) nor does it check bounds for length or `end` relative to the string. Therefore, the condition for `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is not avoided in either call. No other exception types are declared in the `substring` documentation.
remark: The `IndexOutOfBoundsException` can be triggered in two scenarios: (1) In the single-argument call (`msg.substring(START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX)`), when `end == -1`, it is thrown if `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` is negative or greater than the length of `msg`. (2) In the two-argument call (`message.substring(START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX, end)`), when `end != -1`, it is thrown if `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` is negative, if `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX > end`, or if `end` exceeds the length of `message`. Since the code lacks any checks or validations on these conditions, the exception remains possible.
